Subject: Unexpected 503s during peak — request for SLA adjudication and credit

Diego —

We saw a significant spike in 503 responses against our checkout API during our dinner peak today (US-East region). Our monitoring indicates a sustained error window starting ~2027-07-28 17:11:32 UTC and ending ~2027-07-28 17:56:48 UTC (approx 45 minutes). That window materially impacted customer checkouts for multiple merchants.

We’ve attached a trace bundle (trace_bundle_fastcart_20270728.tar.gz) that includes sampled requests, headers, and our client-side retry behavior. Can you confirm receipt and advise next steps for an SLA adjudication and potential credit? We need the official impacted window confirmation and an estimated timeline for a postmortem.

Also copying Procurement to begin the credit conversation.

Thanks,
Jonathan Smith

Diego — initial verification below.

What we found: 
- Ingress logs (us-east-1 / west1) show a sustained 5xx spike starting at 2027-07-28T17:11:32Z and tapering to baseline at 2027-07-28T17:56:48Z. Error rate peaked at ~18% for the checkout route.
- Preliminary root cause: an autoscaler rollout triggered a transient preemption loop on a shard serving the checkout model; the fallback routing did not rehydrate cache quickly which amplified tail errors.
- No evidence of malicious traffic; consistent with internal scaling state.

Attachments staged: west1_5xx_sample.log (2.1MB), k8s-events-snapshot.json (850KB) — uploaded to incident Drive folder.

Recommendation for remedy calculation: use the standard prorated approach outlined in our SLA: calculate percentage downtime of the billing period for the impacted service-group and apply that proportion to the monthly invoice for July. Preliminary ballpark: given the 45-minute window relative to the billing month, we estimate ~10% of a single-month invoice for the reserved capacity tier that covered the affected capacity (I will confirm exact dollars after we reconcile merchant scoping).

Next steps: 
- I’ll finalize the telemetry bundle and post a sanitized log package to Drive by EOD UTC.
- Propose a postmortem meeting with FastCart SREs and Redwood infra: Thu, Jul 29, 09:00–09:45 PT (let me know if that works).

Laura Bennett
Sr. SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Jonathan / Procurement team —

Thanks for your patience. Per our telemetry reconciliation and Laura’s verification, we confirm the impacted window as: 2027-07-28T17:11:32Z through 2027-07-28T17:56:48Z (UTC). This matches the traces you provided and our ingress/back-end logs.

Eligibility and proposed remedy: 
- The event meets our SLA availability breach criteria for the affected service-group and therefore qualifies for a prorated credit.
